trickyParts: up.test.sh sources up.sh minus its last line, so every top-level readonly runs at source time before the test exports SMOKE_PROJECT; the container name therefore cannot be a top-level readonly. It is derived in main() and passed to ensure_nats as $1 (a `readonly` inside main would also break the test, which calls main() four times).

up.test.sh stubs ensure_nats in its main() cases, so the record file is written by main() itself (beside webhook-mode), not by ensure_nats -- that is what lets the test assert the record without docker.
down.sh keeps the record after teardown on purpose: deleting it would make the next down.sh fall back to legion-smoke-nats, a container that may belong to an older rig still running.

forTester: Acceptance 2 is yours: two rigs with different SMOKE_PROJECT, SMOKE_DIR, NATS_PORT, ENVOY_PORT, LEGION_DAEMON_PORT started concurrently, both reaching the controller-alive check; docker ps before and after each down.sh quoted in the PR body's E2E line, showing each removes only its own legion-smoke-nats-<slug>. Negative control suggestion: run down.sh from a SMOKE_DIR whose nats-container record names the *other* rig's container -- it will remove that one (the record is trusted), so instead use a malformed record (e.g. 'not-a-rig-container') and observe the refusal warning with both containers still in docker ps. Round 2 (acceptance 5): re-run the two rigs with adjacent daemon ports (e.g. 19381 and 19382) -- the second up.sh must now refuse before launching anything with `error: Legion daemon worker stream port 19382 is already in use` (or the first, depending on which binds first), and nothing of the refused rig starts; with non-adjacent ports both rigs come up as before. Round 3 (acceptance 6 and 7): from YOUR OWN rig's SMOKE_DIR only. (6) With your rig up, run down.sh from a fresh empty SMOKE_DIR with SMOKE_PROJECT set to your project: it must print `… has no legion.yaml: this directory never started a rig` and your rig's tmux server and container must survive (tmux -L legion-<slug> has-session; docker ps). Then run down.sh from the rig's real SMOKE_DIR with SMOKE_PROJECT exported as some other project: the disagreement warning prints and YOUR rig is torn down. (7) Start a second up.sh into a fresh SMOKE_DIR with your live rig's daemon port (refused at the port check) -- no nats-container file appears in that SMOKE_DIR.
